Ask financial adviser Warren Ingram what goes wrong in stokvels, and he says almost every problem comes down to one thing: nothing was written down. No rule for what happens if someone stops paying, for who can leave and when, or for how the payout works. The second risk is where the money sits: in one person's own bank account, it is exposed to anything that happens to that person, from theft to death, divorce or debts. If the treasurer passes away, the stokvel's money can get tied up in their estate.

Full guide: "Stokvels Explained: How to Protect Your Stokvel Money (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
